root_idea.summary: The root centers on strength, force, and firmness, with related developments involving support, reinforcement, and securing or covering.
root_idea.development: The evidence connects strengthening with tightening or girding, while also preserving independent branches for clothing, covering, vigorous growth, and mutual support.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested Form IV verb is a distinct public verbal form.
The Quran-attested noun is displayed under its normalized citation form أَزْر.

senses.usage_conditions: A transitive use; in the Quranic occurrence, the object is strengthened within the parable of growing vegetation.
In the Quranic expression اشدد به أزري, the possessive form denotes the speaker’s strength or sustaining power.

senses.definition: The back, as the bodily seat or support of strength.
senses.usage_conditions: In اشدد به أزري, this is an explicitly attested interpretation of the construction alongside the interpretation “strengthen my strength.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: To surround or encompass something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I verbal use, including surrounding a thing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strengthen the lower part or foundation of a building.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I construction referring specifically to reinforcing a building at its base.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To clothe or wrap someone with an izar.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form II causative use involving the garment إِزَار.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cover a surface or area.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of herbage covering the ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To reinforce or strengthen a person or thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Especially used of casing and strengthening the lower part of a wall, but also used more generally.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To aid, assist, help, or strengthen someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form III lexical use, including mutual or directed assistance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of vegetation, to become tangled or luxuriant, with one part reaching and strengthening another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form III use describing mutually reinforcing growth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To equal, match, or correspond to something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form III comparative or relational construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To grow strong or vigorous; of vegetation, to grow tall and luxuriant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form V use describing the subject’s becoming strong; the evidence also relates it to being strengthened or having one’s support tightened.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put on or wear an izar.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form VIII reflexive or intransitive clothing use; the form is also transmitted as اِيتَزَرَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Weakness or infirmity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A contrary signification reported for the noun; it is also reflected in one interpretation of the Quranic strengthening expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Aid, assistance, or help.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use distinct from the noun’s sense of strength.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The place or part of either flank where an izar is tied.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical and clothing-related noun use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular manner or mode of putting on or wearing an izar.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun describing the manner in which the garment is worn.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A waist-wrapper or other covering garment; by extension, anything used to veil, conceal, or cover.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The garment may cover the lower body or be understood more generally as a covering.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In a figurative girding expression, to prepare oneself for an affair or to abstain from sexual intercourse in preparation for religious service.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic extension associated with girding or tightening the izar.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Continence or chastity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use in expressions describing someone as having a clean or good izar.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One’s wife, oneself, or one’s wife and family, by metonymy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The exact referent varies among the reported idiomatic explanations.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A ewe.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized lexical use also associated with the call إِزار إِزار used when calling a ewe to be milked.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Describing a horse or mare whose hindquarters or thighs are white, as though marked by an izar.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjective describing the distribution of the animal’s coloring.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A ewe or she-goat black in the hindquarters, as though wearing a black izar.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative passive-participial adjective based on the appearance of the animal’s coloring.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Effective and powerful aid.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative passive-participial expression for assistance made strong or effective.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Form I meaning: surround or encompass.
Reinforcing a wall by casing its lower part.
Form III aid, assistance, and strengthening.
Back and the alternative strength or weakness interpretations of the Quranic construction.
Flank or tying-place for the izar.
Garment, covering, and figurative girding expressions.
Metonymic reference to wife, self, or family.
Adjective for a horse or mare with white hindquarters or thighs.
Animal described as marked like an izar.
Pointer to a form under another root, وزر.

cautions: The noun أَزْر is reported with contrary senses of strength and weakness; the Quranic occurrence is explained primarily as strength, with a separate back interpretation of the same construction.

The public verb is identified by QAC as Form IV آزرَ. The same surface form is treated as a Form III lexical entry in part of the Classical evidence, so that related evidence is retained separately rather than silently changing the Quranic morphology.
The evidence discusses آزر in Quran 6:74 as a proper name, but no corresponding QAC form group or occurrence is supplied here; it is not counted as a third Quranic form.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: Mufradat explicitly discusses the proper name آزر in 6:74, including competing explanations of its origin or meaning, but the supplied QAC packet contains no matching form group or word location for that item.
Mufradat mentions وازر/وزير while explicitly assigning that branch to the root beginning with و; the ministerial sense is therefore not assigned to أزر.
